title: くらい／ぐらい — about ～, to the extent of ～
summary: Has two uses: an approximate quantity, and showing the degree of a state through an example. It follows nouns, numbers, and the plain form of verbs and adjectives. ぐらい is the same as くらい.

body.p: After time, number or money it means 'about that much': 十分くらい, 二十個くらい. Note that ごろ is used for clock times while くらい is for lengths of time and quantities.
In 立てないくらい痛い or 泣きたいくらい悲しい, the first part shows how strong the second is. Nearly the same as ほど, but くらい is more conversational. これくらい and それくらい can also mean 'such a small thing.'

examples.ja: 駅（えき）まで歩（ある）いて十分（じゅっぷん）くらいです。
examples.romaji: Eki made aruite juppun kurai desu.
examples.tr: It's about ten minutes' walk to the station.

examples.ja: 箱（はこ）の中（なか）には、りんごが二十個（にじゅっこ）くらい入（はい）っていた。
examples.romaji: Hako no naka ni wa, ringo ga nijukko kurai haitte ita.
examples.tr: There were about twenty apples in the box.

examples.ja: 立（た）てないくらい、足（あし）が痛（いた）い。
examples.tr: My leg hurts so much that I can't stand up.

pitfalls: For clock times use ごろ (三時ごろ); 三時くらい can sound a little off.
くらい and ぐらい mean the same; use whichever is easier to say.
